_about: Geometry engine profile. 'ranges' are the sizes the rules use, measured on the drawings listed in _source (Phase 1 survey: X marks matched to the text engine by overlap, plus crops checked by eye). 'rules' is written by geolearn.py: for each rule, how often its finding matched the text engine at the same place (agree of n) and, where disagreements were checked by eye, how many of those were in fact right (verified). Confidence = 95% lower bound of that rate (geoengine.confidence).

identify._about: What the geometry engine reports. Only these, and only from these rules; every other finding (rooms, toilets, unclassified shapes) is worked out internally but not reported. Never a shaft, a lift, a window, a cut-out, a column or a void (2026-10-16, final): those six are Step 3's - every X mark decided once by the X sequence (xplace.py) - and Step 5 and the final drawing take them from Step 3. An X mark or a lift-size square is read only as evidence: the place of an X is no room, lift wells along both longer sides make a lift lobby (or a machine room when none of them has a door onto it), flights either side of a long X make a staircase. STAIRCASE: tread lines in flights, or flights either side of an X-marked well (the well is Step 3's void, not reported). LIFT_LOBBY: an enclosed space with lift wells along both longer sides. To report another kind later, add it here with the rules that find it.

LIFT_LOBBY.label: Lift Lobby
LIFT_LOBBY._about: An enclosed space with lift wells along both of its longer sides (within lift_lobby_side_reach_mm of the side - a wall's thickness and the lift door recess). Written on AI_LIFTLOBBY.

MACHINE_ROOM.label: Machine Room
MACHINE_ROOM._about: A space between lift wells (as a lift lobby) where none of the lifts has a door onto it: a door object or swing at the lift, or an opening of at least lift_door_min_mm in the lift's wall facing the space. Written on AI_MACHINEROOM.

SERVICE_LOBBY.label: Service Lobby
SERVICE_LOBBY._about: The polygon a staircase's door opens into (the smallest one within a door leaf of the hinge). A lift with a door onto it is marked as its service lift. Written on AI_SERVICELOBBY; its area goes under SERVICE LOBBY in the area statement.

ranges._lift_side_mm: Lift X marks: p10-p90 2000-2650 mm square on 10 drawings; 341 square X marks of 2.2-2.8 m were lifts 96% of the time.
ranges._void_min_sqm: All 6 X marks of 30 sq.m and more were voids (2 drawings); X marks of 8-30 sq.m were large shafts (21 of 22).
ranges._thin_strip_max_mm: 300 mm wide X strips were riser cupboards (behind a door) or slab cut-outs (along a larger shaft).
ranges._stair_well: X families 600x3300, 800x2900, 1000x3100, 1200x3300 (98 X marks, 8 drawings) were the open well between two stair flights in 9 of 9 crops checked. XA 37th floor: a 446 x 2600 well between two flights of 8 treads (lower bound 400).
ranges._staircase_sqm: Staircases measured 4.4-5.7 x 6.1-8.1 m, 28-47 sq.m (p10-p90, 9 drawings).
ranges._lift_lobby: A lift lobby: an enclosed space between lift_lobby_min_sqm and lift_lobby_max_sqm with a lift well within lift_lobby_side_reach_mm of each of its two longer sides.
ranges._service_lobby_min_width: A service lobby must hold a square this wide somewhere inside it; a wall cavity wrapping a staircase (about 300 mm) does not.
ranges._lift_door: A lift has a door onto a space when a door object or swing stands at it, or its wall facing the space has an opening of at least lift_door_min_mm (wall lines within lift_door_wall_band_mm of its side; area-plan and finish lines do not count, nor does what is drawn in the opening - a landing door, its frame, an elevation of the car on an ELEV / DOOR layer: an opening in the structure is a door). A space between lift wells is a lift lobby when at least lift_lobby_door_share of those lifts have a door onto it (lifts between two lobbies open onto one, so about half do); otherwise it is their machine room.

verified._about: Disagreements with the text engine checked by eye in the Phase 1 crops (2026-10-01): [right, checked, what was seen].
stair_treads: staircases the text engine had not drawn (A-108, A-109, A-106, 285, P14, T1): all real staircases
stair_well_both_sides: X between two stair flights that the text engine called 'Unknown Shaft': all stair wells
lift_square_bank: lift-size X in a bank named otherwise (T1 'Unknown Shaft' lift bank, P14 'SHAFT WELL' in a lift row): 7 lift wells, 2 unclear
toilet_fixtures: fixture clusters with no text toilet: 7 inside real toilet blocks (boundary only a part), 2 wheelchair symbols
